_meta.indication: Treatment of moderate-to-severe primary Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS) in adults

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 12-week parallel-group trial comparing gabapentin enacarbil 1200 mg daily to placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with moderate to severe RLS
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline in IRLS total score and proportion of CGI-I responders
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change in IRLS score at Week 12 was -13.2 (gabapentin enacarbil) vs -8.8 (placebo), p=0.0003; CGI-I responders 76.1% vs 38.9%, p<0.0001

pivotal_trials.design: Three-arm, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 12-week trial comparing gabapentin enacarbil 600 mg and 1200 mg daily to placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with moderate to severe RLS
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline in IRLS total score and proportion of CGI-I responders
pivotal_trials.n: 325 randomized (113 gabapentin enacarbil 1200 mg, 115 gabapentin enacarbil 600 mg, 97 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change in IRLS at Week 12: -13.8 (600 mg) and -13.0 (1200 mg) vs -9.8 (placebo); 600 mg vs placebo p<0.0001, 1200 mg vs placebo p<0.002. CGI-I responders 72.8% (600 mg) and 77.5% (1200 mg) vs 44.8% (placebo), both p<0.0001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10% and at least 2x placebo) were somnolence/sedation and dizziness. In 12-week RLS studies at 600 mg/day, somnolence/sedation occurred in 20% (vs 6% placebo) and dizziness in 13% (vs 4% placebo).
target_moa: Gabapentin enacarbil is a prodrug of gabapentin; its therapeutic effects in RLS are attributable to gabapentin, which binds with high affinity to the α2δ subunit of voltage-activated calcium channels (precise mechanism in RLS unknown).

rems.type: FDA determined it is not necessary for the Medication Guide to be part of a REMS; the Medication Guide is part of the approved labeling under 21 CFR 208 rather than a REMS.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee because the safety profile is acceptable for RLS and the clinical study design is similar to previously approved products in the class.

summary.text: NDA 022399 was submitted under section 505(b)(2) with Neurontin as the reference listed drug; after a Complete Response action in February 2010 over pancreatic acinar cell tumor findings, it was approved in 2011 for moderate-to-severe primary RLS without referral to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated January 8, 2009, received January 9, 2009, submitted pursuant to section 505(b)(2) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Horizant (gabapentin enacarbil) Extended-Release Tablets 600 mg.

Background: The Office of Drug Evaluation-I took a Complete Response action to the original New Drug Application (NDA) submission on 2/17/10, based on findings of pancreatic acinar cell tumors in a 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats.

Your application for Horizant was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile is acceptable for RLS and the clinical study design is similar to previously approved products in the class.
